post.caption: Tiffany's emerald had no buyer for years. The Hooker Emerald weighs 75.47 carats and comes from Colombia. A legend says a sultan once wore it in a belt buckle. Tiffany bought it at auction in 1911 and set it in a tiara, which found no buyer for decades. In 1950, Tiffany reset it as a platinum brooch with 109 round diamonds and 20 baguettes, and it led that year's Christmas catalogue. Janet Annenberg Hooker bought it in 1955 and gave it to the Smithsonian in 1977. It is kept in the Hooker Hall at the museum in Washington.
